evidence.paraphrase: Hager begins contemplating killing his partner.
evidence.quote: And then he found himself toying with the thought of murdering Cahill.

evidence.paraphrase: Hager reasons that delaying the journey will let exposure to cold kill the sick Cahill without visible marks.
evidence.quote:
If Hager were simply to delay in reaching the settlement, Cahill would
die as surely as though from the thrust of a knife or the impact of a
bullet. Exposure to the biting cold would finish him.

evidence.paraphrase: Hager devises a deliberate zigzag route to waste time while appearing to travel.
evidence.quote:
It was his plan to keep zigzagging, approaching the
stream and then retreating, always at a tangent. A great deal of time
would be consumed in this way, with very little actual forward
progress toward Moose Gulch.

evidence.paraphrase: Cahill realizes and accuses Hager of deliberately stalling to kill him.
evidence.quote:
"You're trying to kill me, Matt. I see it
now. You aren't going straight toward Moose Gulch. You're tracking
back and forth to waste time. You ... want me to die!"

evidence.paraphrase: The dying Cahill vows revenge against Hager.
evidence.quote:
"You aren't going to get away with this, Matt. I ... I'm going to get
you. I'm going to make you pay."

evidence.paraphrase: After the murder, an inexplicable cold begins following Hager and worsening.
evidence.quote:
The cold remained with him in the days that followed. It not only
remained. It grew more unbearable.

evidence.paraphrase: Hager alone feels a cold that others cannot perceive, even in warm places.
evidence.quote:
Even near hot stoves, or in heated rooms, he felt
chilled. No one else seemed to notice it. The cold seemed intended for
him alone.

evidence.paraphrase: The materialist Hager acknowledges being haunted by an unnatural cold.
evidence.quote:
He was materialistic. He didn't believe in ghosts. But he knew that
he was being haunted by an unnatural cold that nobody else seemed
able to feel.

evidence.paraphrase: Hager seeks a medical examination to explain the cold.
evidence.quote:
In Los Angeles he yielded to a wild impulse and visited a doctor. He
explained his symptoms, omitting their true cause, and pleaded for
help.

evidence.paraphrase: A doctor finds no physical cause for Hager's symptoms.
evidence.quote:
"I can't understand it," he told Hager. "There's nothing
seriously wrong with you. All you need is plenty of food and rest.
You're probably just imagining things."

evidence.paraphrase: Despite traveling to warmer climates, the cold afflicting Hager intensifies.
evidence.quote:
The climate grew increasingly mild and balmy as he progressed
southward. But the chill that always surrounded him grew worse.

evidence.paraphrase: A priest attempts to exorcize the supernatural cold.
evidence.quote: The priest nodded gravely and began his task.

evidence.paraphrase: The exorcism temporarily succeeds in relieving Hager.
The priest refuses further aid, saying a vision reveals Hager must pay for his crime.
evidence.quote:
"The _padre_ say he no can help you, _senor_. He say he
have how you call vision. It tell him you must pay."

evidence.paraphrase: Despite warmth and fire, Hager freezes to death.
evidence.quote:
It had been a warm night. The fire had been, hot, the blankets
numerous and thick. Yet Hager had _frozen_ to death.

evidence.paraphrase: Even in warm Mexico, Hager cannot feel any warmth.
evidence.quote:
Several days later found him in Mexico. It was warm--but he didn't
feel it. He knew with a terrible certainty that he would never feel
warmth again.
